text:
jess: FYI ACME infra just hit intermittent failures in the POC streaming tests — looks like the corporate proxy is dropping TLS session resume and reusing connections, leading to 502 / ECONNRESET from our SDK. They want a quick workaround and asked whether reserved capacity avoids this. :grimacing:

sam: can you paste the client logs & sample curl that reproduces it? also which SDK and version?

jess: sending cropped logs below from their sysadmin. SDKs: python 1.4.2 and ts 2.0.0 (streaming). Logs: 
```
TLS error: TLS session resumption failed: bad_sess_ticket
proxy 10.10.0.5: connection reset by peer
upstream read: 502 Bad Gateway
```

maria: (ACME) the proxy is an F5 appliance, they said recent firmware changed session-ticket handling. We can reproduce within their network consistently when streaming > ~30s.

sam: ok likely session ticket resumption + connection pool reuse + long-lived streaming = brittle. Short-term workaround: disable connection pooling/keepalive on client so each request creates a new TLS handshake (not ideal for perf). For Node/TS try: 
```
// node-fetch / http.Agent example
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: false });
fetch(url, { agent });
```
For Python requests: 
```
s = requests.Session()
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=0, pool_maxsize=0))
# or set session.close() after each stream
```

alex: another option: reduce per-request stream duration (heartbeat chunks) or short retries with backoff when ECONNRESET occurs. Also try forcing TLS renegotiation by disabling session resumption on client: not always exposed, but connection-recreate works.

jess: ACME wants a config we can ship to them quickly and also asked if dedicated capacity would bypass their proxy — they run everything through the proxy so dedicated won’t help by itself. They asked about a private deployment (VPC) option.

sam: clarify: Hosted API traffic still exits our public endpoints, so corporate proxy will still touch it. Private (VPC or on-prem) would allow us to place the service inside their network or peer directly, avoiding the corporate proxy. For immediate POC we should give the client the client-side workaround + a short-term support plan.

maria: can you confirm security implications? their security team sent a questionnaire asking if we support mTLS between client and our endpoint for POC traffic.

alex: for hosted we don’t support customer mTLS to the public endpoint; we do support TLS + IP allowlist + private options. For Private deployments we can enable mTLS & KMS integration. I'll attach the relevant doc link (later).

jess: pricing question from procurement: if they move to Private (VPC) for the POC month, what's ballpark pricing? need a quick number for procurement to approve access.

sam: ballpark: POC Private single-node reserved for 1 month = "engineering estimate" ~$12k-18k depending on GPU & SLA — I'll ask infra to confirm. Mark as estimate and route to sales AE.

deploy-bot: scheduled run: created temporary POC node (dev) for customer acme-poc-1977, expires in 7 days.

jess: action items: 1) send Python + TS snippets to ACME to disable keepAlive / recreate connections (we'll include simple wrapper), 2) give procurement the ballpark estimate with caveat, 3) schedule a quick call with ACME infra + our eng (sam + alex) to validate F5 config.

sam: I'll prep a tiny reproducible script and a test endpoint to verify retries + connection recreate. putting notes in the support ticket.

alex: short reproducible for TS (stream chunking + forced reconnect): 
```
const opts = { agent: new https.Agent({ keepAlive: false }), timeout: 45000 };
// reconnect logic on 'error' or non-2xx
```

maria: thanks — we'll try the keepAlive=false approach today and report back by EOD. Appreciate the quick swim. :pray:

jess: thanks all, I’ll send the snippets and the estimate to acme procurement now.

sam: ping me on the call, I'll bring logs and a test harness.

(more follow-up will be in the support ticket)
